officials.name: Karen Watford
officials.address: 913 N. Greensboro Street, Lexington, North Carolina 27292
officials.bio: Chair Watford has been married to Samuel Watford of Thomasville for 40 years, has two daughters, Jordan Lupton and Morgan Watford, and two grandchildren, Owen and Leah. She is a graduate of East Davidson High School, attended Elon College, and graduated with a B.A. degree in English from the University of NC at Greensboro. Chair Watford taught for the Davidson County Schools from 1974-2011.

officials.name: Todd Yates
officials.bio: Todd Yates, born in 1965 in Denton, North Carolina, is a fourth-generation resident of Davidson County. He enjoys boating, camping, cooking, traveling, and reading, and currently resides in the Holly Grove Community. Yates is a past member of the Denton Jaycees and has held a private pilot license.

officials.name: Chris Elliott
officials.address: 913 N. Greensboro Street, Lexington, North Carolina 27292
officials.bio: Commissioner Chris Elliott resides in the Central Davidson community and has been married for 15 years to Shannon Elliott. They have two children Mason and Riley Elliott. Commissioner Elliott is an active member of Madison Heights Freewill Baptist Church and also serves as Associate Youth Pastor.

officials.name: Fred McClure
officials.address: 913 N. Greensboro Street, Lexington, North Carolina 27292
officials.bio: Commissioner Fred McClure was born in Tulsa, Oklahoma, and resides in the Welcome community. He served in the United States Air Force and Navy, including two tours in Vietnam, before opening McClure Insurance Group in 1975. He has served multiple non-consecutive terms as a Davidson County Commissioner since 1994 and is a Past-President of the NCACC.

officials.name: Matt Mizell
officials.address: 913 N. Greensboro Street, Lexington, North Carolina 27292
officials.bio: Commissioner Matt Mizell was raised in the town of Midway and now lives in the Arcadia community with his wife. He is a graduate of North Davidson High School and earned a B.A. in Political Science from High Point University, followed by a Master’s in Education and an MBA from Wake Forest University.

officials.name: Steve Shell
officials.bio: Commissioner Steve Shell's family settled in Davidson County in 1752. He has two sons, four grandchildren, and is married to Linda Craver Shell. He attended DDCC and Forsyth Tech, and received special career training from the US Department of Justice and the US Secret Service.

officials.name: Dr. Mike Lee
officials.address: 200 East Main Street, Second Floor Durham, NC 27701
officials.bio: Dr. Michael 'Mike' Lee was first elected to serve as County Commissioner in 2024 and is currently serving his first term. He was sworn in on December 2, 2024. Lee was voted Chair in 2025. He previously served as Vice Chair.

officials.name: Nida Allam
officials.address: 200 East Main Street, Second Floor Durham, NC 27701
officials.bio: Commissioner Nida Allam is Vice Chair of the Durham Board of County Commissioners. Commissioner Nida Allam was sworn in on December 7, 2020. She formerly was the Chair of the BOCC from 2023 to 2025.

officials.name: Michelle Burton
officials.address: 200 East Main Street, Second Floor Durham, NC 27701
officials.bio: Michelle Burton was first elected to serve as County Commissioner in 2024 and is currently serving her first term. She was sworn in on December 2, 2024.

officials.name: Stephen Valentine
officials.address: 200 East Main Street, Second Floor Durham, NC 27701
officials.bio: Stephen J. Valentine was first elected to serve as County Commissioner in 2024 and is currently serving his first term. He was sworn in on December 2, 2024.

officials.name: Wendy Jacobs
officials.address: 200 East Main Street, Second Floor Durham, NC 27701
officials.bio: Commissioner Jacobs is currently in her fourth term with the BOCC, having been first elected in 2012. She served as Vice Chair of the Board of County Commissioners from 2020-2023 and as Chair from 2016-2020.

officials.name: Gloria D. Whisenhunt
officials.bio: Gloria Whisenhunt has been a Forsyth County Commissioner since 1996, serving as both Vice Chair and Chair. Prior to this, she served on the Winston-Salem/Forsyth County Board of Education from 1990-1996. A retired cosmetologist, she decided to run for school board after her son left for college.

officials.name: Dan Besse
officials.bio: Dan Besse is an at-large Commissioner for Forsyth County, a former city council member, and a legal aid attorney. He earned his Political Science degree and law degree from UNC Chapel Hill, and has worked extensively in public health and environmental law. He served on the Winston-Salem City Council from 2001-2020 and was elected to the Board of County Commissioners in 2022.

officials.name: Malishai Woodbury
officials.bio: Malishai "Shai" Woodbury was elected as a county commissioner for District A in 2022, after serving on the Winston-Salem/Forsyth County Board of Education from 2018-2022. A native of Winston-Salem, she has worked as an educator for more than 25 years and earned her doctorate in Education Leadership.

officials.name: Tonya D. McDaniel
officials.bio: Tonya D. McDaniel assumed the position of County Commissioner for District A in 2018, holding a Bachelor of Arts in Political Science and a Masters in Public Administration. During her tenure, she has focused on promoting equity in property tax rates and county funding for school systems, inspired by her god-mother, the late community leader Earline Parmon. She also serves on various committees, including the North Carolina State Health Coordinating Council and the National Association of Counties Veterans & Military Services Committee.

officials.name: G. Gray Wilson
officials.bio: G. Gray Wilson is a full-time practicing trial lawyer in Winston-Salem for 47 years, an author, and a fellow of the American College of Trial Lawyers. He has served as president of both the North Carolina Bar Association and the North Carolina State Bar, and is focused on supporting law enforcement, combating crime, and addressing housing and economic development in Forsyth County.

officials.name: Chad Brown
officials.bio: Chad Brown is a former professional baseball player and lifelong conservative Republican. He began his political career as mayor of Stanley and is currently serving his fourth term on the County Board of Commissioners, having served six years as chairman.

officials.name: Allen Fraley
officials.bio: Allen Fraley has served on the Gaston County Board of Commissioners since 2004, also representing the board on the Gaston/Cleveland/Lincoln Metropolitan Planning Organization. He is the general manager for the Cherryville ABC Board and a licensed Realtor, previously owning an insurance business. Married to Susan for 35 years, he has two children and two grandchildren, and is an active member of the First United Methodist Church in Cherryville.

officials.name: Cathy Cloninger
officials.bio: Cathy Cloninger is a lifelong resident of Gaston County with 34 years of service, primarily in domestic violence advocacy, before her retirement in 2017. In 2022, she was elected as a Dallas Township Commissioner and served one year as Vice-Chair of the Board. She holds a Bachelor’s degree in Social Work and has received numerous awards for her public service and dedication to the community.

officials.name: Jim Bailey
officials.bio: Jim Bailey is a Gaston County native who served in the US Air Force for over two decades, including deployments in Desert Storm and Afghan Freedom. He then had a distinguished 30-year career in Law Enforcement at the Gaston County Sheriff's Office, becoming the first deputy sheriff from Gaston County to attend the FBI National Academy. Currently, he works as a training coordinator and is married with two adult children.

officials.name: Scott Shehan

128 W. Main Ave. Gastonia, NC 28052
P.O. Box 1578 Gastonia, NC 28053-1578

officials.bio: Scott Shehan is a native of Gaston County and a lifelong citizen of Gastonia. After graduating from North Gaston High School in 1998, he attended Appalachian State University. He is an entrepreneur, having started his first business in 1994, and also manages multiple rental properties and owns Silas Ridge Farms, LLC.

officials.name: Tom Keigher
officials.bio: Commissioner Keigher lives in Gastonia with his wife, Donna, and has four adult children and three grandchildren. He graduated from Belmont Abbey College with a degree in Education and has a background in teaching, business, and insurance. He has served on the Gaston County Board of Commissioners for seven terms, including multiple times as chairman and vice-chairman, and is actively involved in numerous state and county boards.

officials.name: Bob Hovis
officials.bio: Bob Hovis is a lifelong resident of Gaston County. He has served on the Gaston County Board of Commissioners since 2016, previously serving as mayor of Bessemer City and on numerous county-appointed advisory boards. He has also been recognized for his volunteerism, including being named Gaston County Volunteer of the Year in 2002, and has been involved with the Bessemer City Chamber of Commerce for nearly four decades.

officials.name: LeAnn Pierce
officials.address: New Hanover County Government Center 230 Government Center Drive Wilmington, NC 28403
officials.bio: LeAnn Pierce was elected to the New Hanover County Board of Commissioners in 2022 and serves as Chair. She previously served as Mayor for the Town of Carolina Beach and owned and operated a hotel for 30 years. She holds a Bachelor of Science degree in Biology from East Carolina University.

officials.name: Dane Scalise
officials.address: New Hanover County Government Center 230 Government Center Drive Wilmington, NC 28403
officials.bio: Dane Scalise was first appointed to the Board of Commissioners in April 2023 and was elected to a four-year term from December 2024 to December 2028, also serving as Vice-Chair from December 2025. He is a husband, father, small business owner, lawyer, and insurance broker, and a graduate of UNC Greensboro and UNC School of Law. Commissioner Scalise has a background in public service, including as Deputy Commissioner of the NC Industrial Commission, and is actively involved in various community boards and pro bono work.

officials.name: Bill Rivenbark
officials.address: New Hanover County Government Center 230 Government Center Drive Wilmington, NC 28403
officials.bio: Commissioner Bill Rivenbark was born and raised in New Hanover County. He is a retired entrepreneur who ran successful businesses in the restaurant and materials management industries and has volunteered extensively in his community, including serving on the New Hanover County Board of Education.

officials.name: Rob Zapple
officials.address: New Hanover County Government Center 230 Government Center Drive Wilmington, NC 28403
officials.bio: Commissioner Rob Zapple and his wife Michele have lived, worked and made a positive contribution in New Hanover County for more than 22 years as community members and small business owners. Rob is a licensed General Contractor, residential and commercial builder, and owner of Rob Zapple Design and Build Inc., and Michele is co-owner of Carolina Gymnastics Academy. He is an advocate for the public process and is active with several non-profit organizations that serve Wilmington and New Hanover County.

officials.name: Stephanie Walker
officials.address: New Hanover County Government Center 230 Government Center Drive Wilmington, NC 28403
officials.bio: Stephanie Walker is a lifelong New Hanover County resident serving her first term as County Commissioner, elected in November 2024. She holds a Bachelor's and Master's degree from UNC Wilmington and previously served four years on the New Hanover County Board of Education.

officials.name: Tim Foster
officials.address: Onslow County Government Center, 234 NW Corridor Boulevard, Jacksonville, NC 28540
officials.bio: Tim Foster was born and raised in Onslow County and began his public service in 1991 as a teacher in the Onslow County School system. He retired in June 2022 after 31 years, having also served as assistant principal and principal, and was selected as the 2018 Onslow County Schools Principal of the year. Commissioner Foster, who holds a B.A. from UNC Wilmington and a Masters from East Carolina University, is currently in his second term.

officials.name: John Davis
officials.address: Onslow County Government Center, 234 NW Corridor Boulevard, Jacksonville, NC 28540
officials.bio: John Davis has been a resident of Swansboro for over 20 years. He and his wife, Jennifer, have been married since 1993 and have three grown children who all graduated from Onslow County Schools. John holds a degree in electrical engineering from NC State University.

officials.name: Lisa Carpenter
officials.address: Onslow County Government Center, 234 NW Corridor Boulevard, Jacksonville, NC 28540
officials.bio: Lisa Carpenter brings an eclectic background to the Board of Commissioners, with decades of business experience in sales, client development, leadership, and training, alongside owning successful businesses and homeschooling her sons. Originally from California, she earned a BA in Economics from the University of California at San Diego and moved to Jacksonville in 2011 after living in various coastal cities. A serious advocate for community involvement, Commissioner Carpenter has served in children's ministries, parent organizations, Boy Scouts leadership, and as president of a local women's political organization, which inspired her to serve on the Onslow County Board of Commissioners.

officials.name: Paul Buchanan
officials.address: Onslow County Government Center, 234 NW Corridor Boulevard, Jacksonville, NC 28540
officials.bio: Paul Buchanan has resided in Onslow County since 1969, serving in the United States Marine Corps and later in public service with the Onslow County Sheriff's Department and Jacksonville Police Department. He is a North Carolina Wesleyan College graduate with a B.S. in Criminal Justice and currently directs Law Enforcement Training at Coastal Carolina Community College. Commissioner Buchanan is an active member of the Onslow County community with his wife, June, and focuses on economic development and youth enrichment programs.

officials.name: Royce Bennett
officials.address: Onslow County Government Center, 234 NW Corridor Boulevard, Jacksonville, NC 28540
officials.bio: Royce Bennett is a Commissioner who works as a Realtor/Broker Associate and has been an independent businessman in Onslow County for over 30 years. He previously served as a police officer and administrator for 12 years and holds a Bachelor of Science Degree in Criminal Justice. He is actively involved in various community organizations and serves on several advisory boards.

officials.name: Tony Padgett
officials.address: Onslow County Government Center, 234 NW Corridor Boulevard, Jacksonville, NC 28540
officials.bio: Tony Padgett is a lifelong resident of Onslow County and a graduate of Jacksonville High School. He served as an Onslow County Commissioner from 1992-2000 and as director of multiple County departments. He advocates for investing in youth, ensuring school safety, and connecting education with local economic needs.

officials.name: Robin Knapp
officials.address: Onslow County Government Center, 234 NW Corridor Boulevard, Jacksonville, NC 28540
officials.bio: Robin Knapp is a former (veteran) USAF officer and retired Supervisory Special Agent/Special Agent with the U.S. Naval Criminal Investigative Service, with 29 years of U.S. Government service. He was assigned to Camp Lejeune, NC, in 1990 and was heavily involved as a coach for local youth programs. Commissioner Knapp is currently serving as the Vice Chairman of the Board of Commissioners and the Commissioner representative to the Juvenile Crime Prevention Committee (JCPC).

officials.name: Earl McKee
officials.bio: Earl McKee is a lifelong resident of Orange County, with a background in agriculture. He was first elected to the Orange County Board of Commissioners in 2010, serving as Board Vice-Chair and Chair, and has been actively involved in various community organizations and boards.

officials.name: Phyllis Portie-Ascott
officials.bio: Phyllis Portie-Ascott, born and raised in Eastern North Carolina, is an entrepreneur who has owned human services businesses and is currently a licensed Real Estate Broker. She has held leadership roles in various political and community organizations, including the Northern Orange Black Voters Alliance and the Orange County Democratic Party, and holds multiple degrees.

officials.name: Sally Greene
officials.bio: A native of Gilmer, Texas, Sally Greene has called Orange County home for three decades. Prior to her election to the Board of County Commissioners in 2018, she served three terms on the Chapel Hill Town Council, demonstrating policy expertise in housing, community development, and criminal justice reform. She holds a J.D. from George Washington University and a Ph.D. in English from UNC-Chapel Hill, and currently works as an associate attorney.

officials.name: Jean Hamilton
officials.bio: Jean Hamilton holds a Ph.D. in Economics from UC Berkeley and a Masters in Social Work from UNC Chapel Hill. She served on the Chapel Hill Carrboro City Schools Board of Education and has been involved in community and public health, later starting a private psychotherapy and counseling practice.

officials.name: Amy Fowler
officials.bio: A lifelong North Carolinian, Amy Fowler, MD, MPH, is a pediatrician at the Chapel Hill Children's Clinic. She earned her M.D. and Master of Public Health from UNC-Chapel Hill and has been invested in improving local education, health, and supports for individuals with disabilities, including serving on the CHCCS Board of Education.

officials.name: Jonathan Lambert-Melton
officials.address: Raleigh Municipal Building, 2nd Floor, 222 W. Hargett St., Raleigh, NC 27601
officials.bio: Jonathan Lambert-Melton has served as an at-large Raleigh City Council member since 2019, where he chairs the Economic Development and Innovation Committee and is Vice-Chair of the Transportation and Transit Committee. An attorney specializing in family law, he is a partner at Soni Brendle Essick Melton and holds degrees from North Carolina State University and North Carolina Central University School of Law. He is the first openly LGBTQ person elected citywide in Raleigh and is a founding board member of Stonewall Sports, Inc.

officials.name: Stormie D. Forte
officials.address: Raleigh Municipal Building, 2nd Floor, 222 W. Hargett St., Raleigh, NC 27601
officials.bio: Stormie Forte was elected as one of two at-large Raleigh City Council members in 2022. Prior to that, she was appointed to represent District D on the Council in 2020. She serves as Vice-Chair of the Housing and Environment Committee and is a member of the Economic Development and Innovation Committee. She currently serves as Mayor Pro Tem.

officials.name: Jane Harrison
officials.office: City Council Member, Mayor Pro Tem
officials.address: Raleigh Municipal Building, 2nd Floor, 222 W. Hargett St., Raleigh, NC 27601
officials.bio: Jane Harrison is serving her second term on Raleigh City Council, representing District D. She was appointed to as the Mayor Pro Tem in December 2025. Council Member Harrison serves as Chair of the Growth and Natural Resources Committee and is a member of the Economic Development and Innovation Committee.

officials.name: Christina Jones
officials.address: Raleigh Municipal Building, 2nd Floor, 222 W. Hargett St., Raleigh, NC 27601
officials.bio: Serving as your District E representative on the Raleigh City Council is one of the greatest honors of my life. I ran for office because I believe city government works best when residents have a real voice in shaping it. My goal has always been to make local government more accessible — to help people understand how decisions are made, who makes them, and how they can get involved.

officials.name: Corey Branch
officials.address: Raleigh Municipal Building, 2nd Floor, 222 W. Hargett St., Raleigh, NC 27601
officials.bio: Corey Branch represents District C and was first elected to the Raleigh City Council in 2015. He serves as Chair of the Community Safety and Quality of Life Committee and as a member of the Transportation and Transit Committee. He served as Mayor Pro Tem from December 2017 to January 2021 and again in 2023.

officials.name: Megan Patton
officials.address: Raleigh Municipal Building, 2nd Floor, 222 W. Hargett St., Raleigh, NC 27601
officials.bio: Megan Patton was elected to represent District B on the Raleigh City Council in 2022. She serves as Chair of the Transportation and Transit Committee and as a member of the Housing and the Environment Committee. Council Member Patton has a B.A. in education from UNC-Chapel Hill and has worked as an elementary school teacher and factory manager.

officials.name: Mitchell Silver
officials.address: Raleigh Municipal Building, 2nd Floor, 222 W. Hargett St., Raleigh, NC 27601
officials.bio: Mitchell Silver was elected in 2024 to represent District A on the Raleigh City Council. He serves on the Housing and Environment Committee and the Community Safety and Quality of Life Committee. Mitchell is an award-winning planner with over 40 years of experience.

officials.name: Janet Cowell
officials.address: Raleigh Municipal Building, 2nd Floor, 222 W. Hargett St., Raleigh, NC 27601
officials.bio: Janet Cowell was elected Mayor of Raleigh in 2024, bringing a deep commitment to public service from her family upbringing. She has a history of elected public service, including as Raleigh city councilor, NC State Senator, and State Treasurer. Prior to being elected Mayor, Janet led the Dix Park Conservancy as President & CEO.
